title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-03-24
source: 10" Betty Board Reel > PCM501ES > Fostex D5 (Jace's tape) optical S/PDIF out > disk

ai_review.summary: Betty‑board recording of excellent sound quality captures a superb ’73 show highlighted by a monster “He’s Gone”, soaring Spanish Jam and a tight Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The Betty‑board source is generally clear, with only occasional hiss or reel‑damage artefacts that can be turned up a bit. Musically the concert is a classic – the second set is described as magical, featuring an unforgettable “He’s Gone” vocal jam, a long Spanish Jam that morphs into a concise Dark Star and a fiery finish with Sugar Magnolia. The first set is solid but a little uneven, with a few shorter jams and some fluffed lyrics.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer stars (mostly 5) and glowing language about performance; recording praised as good‑to‑excellent with only minor technical quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Betty board capture is crisp and well‑balanced, less hiss than many audience tapes. A few SQ issues (mold/water damage on reels) cause occasional volume drops or hiss; overall listenable and enjoyable.

poor_songs: Mind Left Body Jam (Mud Love Buddy)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts strong but wanders a bit before building momentum; the second set is a continuous high‑energy flow with seamless segues (China>Rider, Truckin'>Spanish Jam>Dark Star>Sing Me Back Home) that keep the magic alive.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring vocals on “He’s Gone”, tight guitar tone and inventive solos; trades brilliantly with Keith and leads the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as heavy, bomb‑dropping bass that locks in perfectly with Bill; provides a solid backbone throughout both sets.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm work and vocal contributions highlighted on Big River, Playin' In The Band and other numbers; his singing is noted as strong and on point.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard work gets kudos for trading with Jerry and “crushing” the JBG jam; adds texture to the jams and transitions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann keeps perfect time, adds flourishes in transitions (e.g., Rider), and drives the high‑energy sections.
